questions.question: A cracked rim should be:

options.text: Moved to one of a pair of dual tires.

questions.explanation: Check your wheels before driving. Look for damage on the wheels and rims. Welded wheels or rims are not safe to use.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer:

options.text: Do not open the trailer doors.
Put a large, heavy blanket over the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not open the trailer doors.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors if there is a cargo fire. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen, which makes it burn faster and hotter.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, you should:

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Do not try to reach your destination while tired—it is dangerous. Coffee cannot replace rest.

questions.question: When putting out an electrical fire, you should:
questions.explanation: B:C extinguishers work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Are only used on trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Help drivers stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) stop wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: Always do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order because:

options.text: You will be less likely to forget something.
You will have more time to complete the inspection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget something.
questions.explanation: Using the same order every time helps you remember all the steps. You are less likely to skip something when you follow the same checklist order.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible inside a trailer.
Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
Placed on the driver's side of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
questions.explanation: A vehicle that is top-heavy is more likely to roll over. Keep cargo weight as low in the trailer as possible.

questions.question: After an accident, flares should be used carefully because:

options.text: Fuel may be spilled on the ground and catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares in sunny weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fuel may be spilled on the ground and catch fire.
questions.explanation: After an accident, spilled fuel can catch fire if flares are used nearby. Use flares carefully.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, a driver should:

options.text: Watch for people getting out of a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for people getting out of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. People may step out without looking for traffic. A parked car may start moving without warning.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up a vehicle and its load. It keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, how many feet does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: When you pull over on the side of the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Always turn on your four-way emergency flashers when you stop on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What sign shows that standing water is on the road?
questions.explanation: Standing water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Clear reflections, tire splashes, or rain drops on the road show that standing water is present.

questions.question: Loading cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Increases the chance of a rollover.
Increases the chance that items will fall down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the chance of a rollover.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity increases the risk that the vehicle will tip over. Always load cargo with safe weight distribution.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will safely fit under a bridge, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an overhead object if you are not sure your vehicle will fit. Take a different route if possible.

questions.question: Knowing what is behind you while driving is:
questions.explanation: Safe driving means knowing what is happening on all sides of your vehicle. Use your mirrors often to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: Why are multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions used?

options.text: To make a vehicle operate more smoothly

questions.explanation: Many vehicles use multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions to provide extra gears.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles use the ____ method to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to change gears.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are safe to use on rear tires.
Are safe to use only with heavy loads.

questions.explanation: Never use wheels or rims that have been welded for repairs.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, decrease your speed. Avoid driving in foggy conditions if possible.
